extracted.intended_audience: Users/developers of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians, computer-algebra programmers) who use its library procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR libraries (solve.lib, triang.lib, ntsolve.lib, zeroset.lib, signcond.lib, graphics.lib, latex.lib) describing usage, assumptions, returns, notes and examples for each procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: simplexOut
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: simplexOut(l); l list. Purpose: the procedure prints the computed solution of simplex (as strings) in a nice format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: l is the output of simplex. Return: Nothing. Example shows creating a matrix for an LP, calling simplex(sm, ...), then simplexOut(sol) which prints z and variable values. See also: simplex.

rubrics_metrics.name: triangLf_solve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: triangLf_solve(i [, p]); i ideal, p integer, p>0 gives precision of complex numbers in digits (default p=30). Purpose: determine recursively all complex roots of zero-dimensional ideal i using a triangular system (Lazard’s Algorithm with factorization) and Laguerre’s algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: ground field has char 0; i is zero-dimensional ideal. Return: ring R with same number of variables but complex coefficients (precision p). R comes with a list rlist containing complex roots. Example: compute intersection points of two curves; the procedure creates ring R; rlist holds complex solutions; to access them use setring R; rlist.

rubrics_metrics.name: triangM_solve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: triangM_solve(i [, p]); i ideal, p integer, p>0: precision of complex numbers (default p=30). Purpose: uses a triangular system (Moeller's Algorithm) computed from a standard basis of input ideal i to determine recursively all complex roots with Laguerre’s algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: ground field char 0; i zero-dimensional ideal. Return: ring R with complex coefficients and list rlist of complex roots. Example provided; access results by setring R; rlist.

rubrics_metrics.name: triangL_solve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: triangL_solve(i [, p]); i ideal, p integer, p>0 gives precision (default p=30). Purpose: uses a triangular system (Lazard’s Algorithm) computed from a standard basis of input ideal i to determine recursively all complex roots with Laguerre’s algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: ground field char 0; i zero-dimensional ideal. Return: ring R with complex coefficients and list rlist of complex roots. Example shows calling triangL_solve(s,10) and retrieving rlist.

rubrics_metrics.name: triang_solve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: triang_solve(l,p [,d]); l list, p,d = integers. Purpose: l is a list of finitely many triangular systems whose union of varieties equals the variety of the initial ideal. p>0 gives precision of complex numbers, d>0 gives precision for near-zero-determination (default d=1/2*p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: ground field char 0; l was computed using Lazard or Moeller algorithms. Return: ring R with complex coefficients and a list rlist of complex roots. Example shows triang_solve(triangLfak(stdfglm(s)),10) and using setring R; rlist to access solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: triangL
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: triangL(G); G = ideal. Purpose: Algorithm of Lazard: given G, the reduced lexicographical Groebner basis of a zero-dimensional ideal (sorted by increasing leading terms), returns a list of finitely many triangular systems whose union of varieties equals variety(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: G is reduced lex Groebner basis of a zero-dimensional ideal. Return: list of triangular systems. Note: references Lazard (1992). Example output shows triangular decompositions for cyclic(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: triangLfak
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: triangLfak(G); G = ideal. Purpose: Lazard algorithm with factorization: returns a list of finitely many triangular systems (each polynomial factorized) whose union of varieties equals variety(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: G is reduced lex Groebner basis of zero-dimensional ideal. Return: list of triangular systems with factorized polynomials. Note: reference Lazard (1992). Example shows numerous factorized triangular systems for cyclic(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: triangM
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: triangM(G[,i]); G = ideal, i = integer. Purpose: Moeller's algorithm: given the reduced lex Groebner basis of a zero-dimensional ideal, returns a list of triangular systems whose union of varieties equals variety(G). If i = 2, then each polynomial of the triangular systems is factorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: G is reduced lex Groebner basis. Return: list of triangular systems. Note: reference Moeller (1993). Example outputs shown for cyclic(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: triangMH
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: triangMH(G[,i]); G = ideal, i = integer. Purpose: Moeller and Hillebrand algorithm: returns a list of triangular systems such that the disjoint union of their varieties equals variety(G). If i = 2 each polynomial of the triangular systems is factorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: G is reduced lex Groebner basis of zero-dimensional ideal. Return: list of triangular systems with disjoint varieties. Note: references Moeller and Hillebrand; examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: nt_solve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: nt_solve(gls,ini[,ipar]); gls, ini = ideals, ipar = list/intvec. Purpose: Real Newton solving of polynomial systems: gls contains equations, ini is ideal of initial approximate solutions; ipar controls max iterations and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ipar default [100,10]; ipar[1] = max iterations; ipar[2] = accuracy. Acceptance: accepts solution sol if ||gls(sol)|| < eps0*(0.1^ipar[2]) where eps0 = ||gls(ini)||. Assume: gls is zero-dimensional ideal with nvars(basering) = size(gls) (>1). Return: ideal coordinates of one solution (if found), 0 else. Note: if printlevel>0 displays comments (default 0). Example shows usage and output numeric solution coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: triMNewton
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: triMNewton(G,a[,ipar]); G,a = ideals, ipar = list/intvec. Purpose: Newton iteration for triangular systems: G is triangular system of n equations in n vars, a is ideal of numbers (approximation), ipar controls iterations and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ipar default [100,10]; ipar[1] = max iterations; ipar[2] = accuracy. Acceptance criterion: accept solution sol if |G(sol)| < |G(a)|*(0.1^ipar[2]) (using absolute norm). Return: an ideal containing coordinates of a better approximation of a zero of G. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Quotient(f, g); f,g are polynomials. Purpose: compute quotient q and remainder r such that f = g*q + r, deg(r) < deg(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering = Q[x] or Q(a)[x]. Return: list [1]=quotient q, [2]=remainder r. Note: This procedure is outdated; use div and mod instead. Example shows computing quotient and remainder in a ring with minpoly.

rubrics_metrics.name: remainder
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: remainder(f, g); f,g are polynomials. Purpose: compute remainder r of division of f by g (f = g*q + r, deg(r) < deg(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering = Q[x] or Q(a)[x]. Return: poly. Note: outdated, use mod/reduce instead. Example shows remainder(x4-1, x3-1) = x-1.

rubrics_metrics.name: roots
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: roots(f); f is a polynomial. Purpose: compute all roots of f in a finite extension of the ground field without multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: ring (polynomial ring over extension) containing list 'theRoots' and polynomials 'newA' and 'f'. 'theRoots' = list of roots (no multiplicities). If ground field is Q(a') and extension is Q(a), 'newA' is representation of a' in Q(a). Assume: ground field is Q or simple extension of Q given by a minpoly. Example demonstrates creation of new ring R1 with theRoots, newA, and f; shows how to setring R1 and access these objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: sqfrNorm
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sqfrNorm(f); f is a polynomial. Purpose: compute the norm of the squarefree polynomial f in Q(a)[x].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: f must be squarefree, basering = Q(a)[x] and minpoly != 0. Return: list [1]=squarefree norm of g (poly), [2]=g (= f(x - s*a)) (poly), [3]=s (int). Note: the norm is an element of Q[x]. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: zeroSet
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: zeroSet(I [,opt]); I = ideal, opt = integer. Purpose: compute the zero-set of a zero-dimensional ideal I in a finite extension of the ground field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: dim(I) = 0 and ground field is Q or simple extension of Q given by a minpoly. Return: ring containing list 'theZeroset' (list of zeros each as an ideal), polynomial 'newA' and ideal 'id' (I in Q(a)[x1,...]). Options: opt=0 no primary decomposition (default); opt>0 primary decomposition. Note: if I contains algebraic number param, I must be transformed w.r.t. 'newA'. Example shows setring T; access minpoly, newA, id, theZeroset and mapping back to basering.

rubrics_metrics.name: egcdMain
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: egcdMain(f, g); f,g are polynomials. Purpose: compute polynomial gcd of f and g over Q(a)[x].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering = Q[x,a] and ideal mpoly is defined (may be 0), representing Q(a)[x] together with its minimal polynomial. Return: poly. Note: outdated, use gcd instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorMain
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: factorMain(f); f is a polynomial. Purpose: compute factorization of squarefree polynomial f over Q(a)[t], minpoly = p(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering = Q[x,a], representing Q(a)[x]; ideal mpoly must be defined (may be 0). Return: list [1]=factors (first is a constant), [2]=multiplicities (not yet implemented). Note: outdated, use factorize instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: invertNumberMain
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: invertNumberMain(f); f is a polynomial. Purpose: compute 1/f if f is a number in Q(a) (represented by polynomial in Q[a]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering = Q[x1,...,xn,a], ideal mpoly must be defined and != 0. Return: poly 1/f. Note: outdated, use / instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: quotientMain
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: quotientMain(f, g); f,g are polynomials. Purpose: compute quotient q and remainder r s.t. f = g*q + r, deg(r) < deg(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering = Q[x,a] and ideal mpoly is defined (may be 0) representing Q(a)[x] with its minimal polynomial. Return: list [1]=quotient q, [2]=remainder r. Note: outdated, use div/mod instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: remainderMain
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: remainderMain(f, g); f,g are polynomials. Purpose: compute remainder r s.t. f = g*q + r, deg(r) < deg(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering = Q[x,a] and ideal mpoly is defined (may be 0). Return: poly. Note: outdated, use mod/reduce instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: rootsMain
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rootsMain(f); f is a polynomial. Purpose: compute all roots of f in a finite extension of the ground field without multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering = Q[x,a] ideal mpoly must be defined (might be 0). Return: list with entries: [1]=roots of f (each entry is polynomial), [2]='newA' representation, [3]=minpoly of algebraic extension. Note: might change ideal mpoly!!

rubrics_metrics.name: sqfrNormMain
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sqfrNorm(f); f is a polynomial. Purpose: compute the norm of the squarefree polynomial f in Q(a)[x].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: f must be squarefree, basering = Q[x,a] and ideal mpoly equals 'minpoly' representing Q(a)[x] together with 'minpoly'. Return: list [1]=squarefree norm (poly), [2]=g (= f(x - s*a)), [3]=s (int). Note: norm is element of Q[x].

rubrics_metrics.name: containedQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: containedQ(data, f [, opt]); data = list; f = any type; opt = integer. Purpose: test if f is an element of data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: int 0 if f not contained in data, 1 if contained. Options: opt=0 use '==' for comparing f with elements from data; opt=1 use sameQ for comparing.

rubrics_metrics.name: sameQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sameQ(a, b); a,b = list/intvec. Purpose: test elementwise equality a == b (i.e., a[i] = b[i]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: int 0 if a != b, 1 if a == b.

rubrics_metrics.name: signcnd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: signcnd(P,I); P,I = ideals. Purpose: determine sign conditions realized by polynomials of P on V(I) and count how many points realize each condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list of two lists: first lists sign conditions, second lists counts; both lists have same length equal to number of sign conditions realized. Assume: I is a Groebner basis. Note: psigncnd does pretty printing. Example: shows interpreting entries (e.g., P[1] > 0, P[2] = 0) and counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: psigncnd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: psigncnd(P,l); P ideal, l list. Purpose: formatted/pretty-printed version of output from signcnd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list (formatted output). Example prints human-readable lines like '1 elements of V(I) satisfy {P[1] = 0,P[2] > 0}' etc. See signcnd.

rubrics_metrics.name: firstoct
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: firstoct(I); I ideal. Purpose: return number of points of V(I) lying in the first octant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I is given by a Groebner basis. Return: number (int). Example: firstoct(i) -> 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: staircase
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: staircase(s,I); s a string, I ideal in two variables. Purpose: produce a string with Mathematica input for displaying staircase diagrams (exponent vectors of initial ideal of I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: ideal I should be given by a standard basis. Let s="" and paste output into a Mathematica notebook. Example shows output Show[Graphics[{...}]]. Also shows usage with fetch to transfer ideal between rings before calling staircase.

rubrics_metrics.name: mathinit
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: mathinit(); Purpose: produce initializing string for loading Mathematica's ImplicitPlot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: mathinit() -> '<< Graphics`ImplicitPlot`' which should be pasted into a Mathematica notebook.

rubrics_metrics.name: mplot
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: mplot(fname, I [,I1,I2,.., s]); fname = string; I,I1,I2,.. = ideals; s = string representing plot region. Purpose: return string text with Mathematica commands to display plot for curves, space curves, surfaces, or implicit curves depending on shape of ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: plotregion defaulted to -1,1 around zero. Conventions: ideal with 2 entries in one variable = parametrised plane curve; 3 entries in one variable = parametrised space curve; 3 entries in two variables = parametrised surface; 2 entries in two variables = implicit curve given as I[1]==I[2]; 1 entry in two variables = implicit curve f == 0. Use ideals I1,I2,.. to produce multiple plots (same number of entries as I). Example shows ParametricPlot and ParametricPlot3D outputs ready to paste into Mathematica.

rubrics_metrics.name: latex.lib global variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Global variables controlling typesetting: TeXwidth, TeXnofrac, TeXbrack, TeXproj, TeXaligned, TeXreplace, NoDollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions: TeXwidth (int) controls breaking of long polynomials (-1,0,1..9,>9). TeXnofrac (int) flag: write 1/2 instead of \frac{1}{2}. TeXbrack (string) controls brackets around ideals and matrices ("{","(","<","|", or empty). TeXproj (int) flag: write ':' instead of ',' in vectors. TeXaligned (int) flag: write maps (and ideals) aligned. TeXreplace (list) entries = 2 strings for replacing symbols. NoDollars (int) flag: suppress surrounding $ signs. Call texdemo() to obtain an explanatory LaTeX2e file texlibdemo.tex.

rubrics_metrics.name: closetex
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: closetex(fname); fname string. Purpose: write a LaTeX2e closing line into file <fname>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: nothing. Note: preceding '>>' are deleted and suffix '.tex' (if not given) is added to fname. Example shows opentex, texobj, closetex usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: opentex
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: opentex(fname); fname string. Purpose: write a LaTeX2e header into a new file <fname>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: nothing. Note: preceding '>>' are deleted and suffix '.tex' is added if not given. Example: opentex('exmpl'); texobj('exmpl','hello'); closetex('exmpl');

rubrics_metrics.name: tex
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tex(fname); fname string. Purpose: call LaTeX (LaTeX2e) to compile the file fname.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: nothing; calls latex2e for <fname>. Note: preceding '>>' are deleted and suffix '.tex' is added if not given. Example demonstrates calling latex and shows pdfTeX output, and cleans temporary files.

rubrics_metrics.name: texdemo
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: texdemo(); Purpose: generate a LaTeX2e file texlibdemo.tex explaining features of latex.lib and its global variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: nothing; generates demo file.

rubrics_metrics.name: texfactorize
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: texfactorize(fname,f); fname string, f poly. Purpose: typeset polynomial factorization for LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fname=="": returns string with f as product of irreducible factors. Otherwise appends string to file <fname> and returns nothing. Note: preceding '>>' deleted and suffix '.tex' is added if not given.
